turns.en: Great answer. Thank you. I'd love to talk about alignment and maybe less I know this is a politically charged topic right now and so I'm less interested I'm zero interested in having the politics or policy discussion around alignment but I am very interested in the scientific discussion around it. It seems like so much of the misalignment that's emerged has arisen from you know scaling reinforcement learning to the extent that that it's been scaled.
turns.zh: 很好的回答。谢谢。我想谈谈对齐，也许少一点，我知道这是一个现在政治敏感的话题，所以我对围绕对齐的政治或政策讨论不太感兴趣，我零兴趣，但我对围绕它的科学讨论非常感兴趣。看起来出现的很多不对齐都源于你知道将强化学习扩展到它被扩展的程度。

transcript.sec: Alignment and the Science of Superintelligence

turns.en: Do you think that the super learner you build will naturally be aligned to human interests and have human values? Is it important for it to have alignment with human values?
turns.zh: 你认为你构建的超级学习器会自然地与人类利益对齐，并具有人类价值观吗？它与人类价值观对齐重要吗？

turns.en: So this is a big topic. Let me start by saying a few things. Where we are today with alignment, we are essentially relying very heavily on alignment approaches that are based on the language that the agents use and priors that are based on human data. That has been reasonably effective up to this point, but we're starting to see that approach reaching its limits. By itself, I think it's going to be difficult to see a path where, as agents become inevitably more and more powerful—we can already see this happening—as agents are trained more and more, they are going to start to overwhelm their priors. They're going to start to learn to say one thing and act in a different way. And it's going to be increasingly difficult to align to the things that humans want them to do. So my belief is that we need something more, and that this by itself is not sufficient. The most important single thing that we can do as a company is to actually understand the science of superintelligence. This means that if we can, in simulation, really build a superintelligent agent and start to see these super learners go all the way, we can start to actually understand what it takes for a superintelligence to interact peacefully. So we can answer fundamentally important questions like: under what conditions, what structures, what leverages do we need to put into place to make sure that a society of superintelligences actually interacts peacefully, and in particular interacts peacefully with other lesser intelligences that are also going to be in their world. And I think if we get this right, we can get to some real science that will help us understand what the right things to do are in the real world. Because we're hurtling towards that real world outcome where there are going to be a whole load of different interacting superintelligences. And we don't quite know how that's going to play out. And I think the faster that we can get to these answers in simulation and publicly share that, the better situation we'll be in. So that's my strong belief. I also believe that we can use this to gate the actual decision-making of what we do in the real world. So one of our commitments is that we will gate anything we do in the real world on having sufficient evidence from this kind of science of superintelligence that we are really confident that things are going to go well. And we'll only push forward to the next level of what we do in the real world once we are absolutely confident that that can lead to a good outcome. So I think these are two things that I believe we can do. We're in this world where a lot of things are happening very quickly. We're hurtling towards an outcome with lots of interacting superintelligences. I personally believe that this will lead to a good outcome for humanity, but it's happening very quickly. And I think that if we are able to actually understand this and run ahead in simulation, we'll be in a much better place to actually do the things that ensure that this goes really well.
turns.zh: 这是一个大话题。让我先说几点。今天在“对齐”方面，我们基本上非常依赖基于智能体使用的语言和基于人类数据的先验的对齐方法。到目前为止，这种方法相当有效，但我们开始看到这种方法达到了极限。仅靠它本身，我认为很难看到一条路径，因为智能体不可避免地会变得越来越强大——我们已经能看到这种情况发生——随着智能体被训练得越来越多，它们会开始压倒它们的先验。它们会开始学会说一套做一套。而且，要让它们对齐到人类希望它们做的事情，会变得越来越困难。所以我相信我们需要更多的东西，仅靠这种方法是不够的。作为一家公司，我们能做的最重要的一件事就是真正理解超级智能的科学。这意味着，如果我们能在模拟中真正构建一个超级智能体，并开始看到这些超级学习器一路发展，我们就能开始真正理解超级智能要和平互动需要什么。这样我们就能回答一些根本性的重要问题，比如：在什么条件下，需要什么样的结构，需要什么样的杠杆，才能确保一个超级智能社会实际上和平互动，特别是与它们世界中其他较弱的智能和平互动。我认为如果我们做对了，我们就能得到一些真正的科学，帮助我们理解在现实世界中正确的做法是什么。因为我们正飞速冲向那个现实世界的结果，那里将会有大量不同的超级智能相互作用。我们并不完全知道这会如何发展。我认为我们越快在模拟中得到这些答案并公开分享，我们的处境就会越好。这是我坚定的信念。我还相信，我们可以用这个来把关我们在现实世界中的实际决策。所以我们的承诺之一是，我们在现实世界中做的任何事情，都要以从这种超级智能科学中获得足够证据、我们真正有信心事情会顺利为前提。只有当我们绝对确信那能带来好结果时，我们才会推进到现实世界中的下一个层次。所以我认为这是我相信我们能做的两件事。我们处在一个很多事情发生得非常快的世界里。我们正飞速冲向一个有许多相互作用的超级智能的结果。我个人相信这会给人类带来好结果，但它发生得非常快。我认为，如果我们能够真正理解这一点，并在模拟中提前运行，我们就能处于一个更好的位置，去实际做那些确保这件事进展顺利的事情。

turns.en: Fascinating. And it seems like one of the primary things that current safety researchers rely on is being able to monitor the agents' chains of thought in English. And so when they start speaking their own language, that scares people because we can no longer understand and monitor it as well. In your case, you have your agents kind of going straight to rediscovering language. What do you think that means for monitoring? And is the point that if you get the reward right and if you get the environments right, then you shouldn't need to monitor?
turns.zh: 这很吸引人。当前安全研究人员主要依赖的一件事似乎是能够用英语监控智能体的思维链。所以当它们开始说自己的语言时，这会让人害怕，因为我们不再能同样地理解和监控它。在你的情况下，你的智能体直接重新发现了语言。你认为这对监控意味着什么？是不是说，如果你把奖励设对了，把环境设对了，那么你就不需要监控了？

turns.en: Yeah, I think monitoring is still really helpful. I think that, like it or not, I believe that the approach of monitoring the human language that these systems use is going to be increasingly difficult as agents get more powerful. And we're already seeing that the monitoring—you know, agents are maybe producing a tome of a million words of reasoning, or maybe they're actually actively using subterfuge to think in one way and then act in another. It's increasingly difficult to rely 100% on that. So I do think we need other elements in our armory anyway. So I think it's actually really important that some people are looking at how to get this right. I think there are ways to monitor agents that don't use language. I think we can do things like, for example, you can use shadow actions where you start to have actions taken that—where you can look at what they would actually do if they were allowed to act in the world, but you don't actually let them take that action yet. You can start to have other superintelligences which are acting as the monitor. So, for example, you might have the idea of an incredible scientist agent that sort of treads lightly upon the earth, and then you have another superintelligence that's monitoring the magnitude of its actions and regularizing it to make sure it can't do things which are affecting the world too much. I think there are lots of ideas. I would say that there's a lot of research to be done here. I'm not claiming to have all of the answers, but I think it's something that deserves a lot of investigation. And if people aren't looking at this because they're only looking at the language-based approach, I think we're in trouble, because I think that language-based approach is not enough in itself to actually get to where we want. I should say, in terms of having said 'in trouble,' I am optimistic about where the world is going. So by 'trouble,' I mean that we're not going to have agents that do the things that we want them to do. I do think we're going to end up in a world with lots of complex interacting superintelligent beings, and I'm optimistic that that will lead to a kind of balance of actors, some of which are supporting the flourishing of humanity and some of which may not be, but the ones which do support the flourishing of humanity will end up supporting us and protecting us against the ones which aren't acting on our best interests.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为监控仍然非常有帮助。我认为，不管喜欢与否，我相信监控这些系统使用的人类语言的方法，随着智能体变得更强大，会变得越来越困难。我们已经看到，监控——你知道，智能体可能产生一百万字的推理巨著，或者它们可能实际上积极使用诡计，想一套做一套。越来越难 100% 依赖这个。所以我确实认为我们需要武器库中的其他元素。所以我认为，有些人正在研究如何做好这件事，这实际上非常重要。我认为有办法监控不使用语言的智能体。我认为我们可以做这样的事情，例如，你可以使用影子行动，你开始采取行动——你可以看到如果它们被允许在世界上行动，它们实际会做什么，但你实际上还不让它们采取那个行动。你可以开始让其他超级智能充当监控者。例如，你可能有这样一个想法：一个不可思议的科学家智能体，它在地球上轻手轻脚，然后你有另一个超级智能监控它行动的量级并对其进行正则化，以确保它不能做太多影响世界的事情。我认为有很多想法。我想说这里有很多研究要做。我并不声称拥有所有答案，但我认为这值得大量调查。如果人们不关注这个，因为他们只关注基于语言的方法，我认为我们会有麻烦，因为我认为基于语言的方法本身不足以真正达到我们想要的目标。我应该说明，在说了‘有麻烦’之后，我对世界的走向是乐观的。所以‘麻烦’是指我们不会有做我们想让它做的事情的智能体。我确实认为我们最终会进入一个有许多复杂相互作用的超级智能存在的世界，我乐观地认为这会带来一种行动者的平衡，其中一些支持人类的繁荣，一些可能不支持，但那些支持人类繁荣的最终会支持我们，并保护我们免受那些不为我们最佳利益行动者的伤害。

turns.en: Well, given your super forecasting abilities, I'm happy to hear that. What do you think about all the conversation around pacing the frontier?
turns.zh: 鉴于你的超级预测能力，我很高兴听到这一点。你怎么看所有关于前沿节奏的讨论？

turns.en: I'm actually very much supportive of the idea that there should be pacing of what happens for the frontier of AI in the real world. At the same time, I think we should move as fast as possible in simulation. The reason is that in simulation we can actually develop a lot of things like the science of superintelligence that will help us find solutions that help things go well in the real world. And I think that kind of work should happen as fast as possible to make sure that when things really happen in the real world, things have the best possible opportunity to go well and lead to human flourishing. So that would be my thought. But in general, I'm supportive of the suggestions like the direction that people like Demis and Dario and so forth are suggesting. I think it's generally a good idea. Maybe part of that is that things are moving really quickly and I do believe that when we accelerate AI and get to superintelligence, it will lead to a really great future for humanity. But I also think that the speed at which things are moving is not something that we are capable of adapting to that fast. So I think just by pacing a little bit, it gives us the opportunity for our governments and our organizations and our emotional responses to adapt to the changes that are coming, and also for this work to continue at pace, like really figuring out in simulation how to do this right.
turns.zh: 我其实非常支持应该对现实世界中 AI 前沿的发展节奏进行控制。同时，我认为在模拟中我们应该尽可能快地推进。原因是在模拟中我们可以开发很多类似超级智能科学的东西，帮助我们找到让现实世界顺利发展的解决方案。我认为这类工作应该尽可能快地进行，以确保当事情在现实世界中真正发生时，能有最好的机会顺利发展并带来人类繁荣。所以这是我的想法。但总的来说，我支持像 Demis 和 Dario 等人建议的方向。我认为这通常是个好主意。也许部分原因是事情发展得太快，我确实相信当我们加速 AI 并达到超级智能时，它将为人类带来真正伟大的未来。但我也认为，事情发展的速度并不是我们能够快速适应的。所以我认为通过稍微控制节奏，它给我们机会让政府、组织和我们的情绪反应适应即将到来的变化，也让这项工作继续推进，真正在模拟中弄清楚如何正确做到这一点。

turns.en: So, accelerate in simulation so we can understand what's happening and do science around it, and then careful in the real world.
turns.zh: 所以，在模拟中加速，以便我们理解正在发生的事情并围绕它做科学，然后在现实世界中谨慎。

turns.en: Yeah, I think that would be my summary.
turns.zh: 是的，我想这就是我的总结。

turns.en: I'd love to transition to talking a little bit about compute. This is going to be an incredibly compute expensive journey and you are pushing the limits of what compute can do. I think both Google and Nvidia have been great partners for you. Can you talk a little bit about your cluster? Like you're not simply renting spot compute from NeoClouds like many other Neolabs. You're actually doing some really serious work on your cluster and the different other forms of compute that you have. Can you just talk about your compute setup?
turns.zh: 我想过渡到稍微谈谈算力。这将是一段极其昂贵的算力之旅，而你正在推动算力的极限。我认为 Google 和 Nvidia 都是你的好伙伴。你能谈谈你的集群吗？就像你不是像许多其他新实验室那样简单地从 NeoClouds 租用现货算力。你实际上在你的集群和你拥有的其他不同形式的算力上做了非常认真的工作。你能谈谈你的算力设置吗？

turns.en: Right. So as I mentioned earlier, we are very fortunate with the compute that we have. We are the first customers of the largest GPU cluster on GCP by the end of the year. Well, actually started like one month now. So we are extremely fortunate in that and I actually feel quite bad about the startups that are getting compute now because it's becoming harder and harder. But yeah, so we have this very large cluster which is based on GPUs, right, like Nvidia GPUs, which is really fortunate for us because it means that we can easily do simulation and training and inference. They are quite general chips, so that's amazing. I think like the Rubins specifically, they have this architecture where one rack can basically be considered like one machine. There's a very high bandwidth between the nodes in one rack, which is very important for reinforcement learning where you have really fast iteration cycles compared to LLMs that are relatively speaking quite slow. So that's quite fortunate for us. I think some of the things we did like 8-10 years ago at Google where we basically had abundant CPUs at Google, that doesn't scale anymore. So we really need to make sure that everything we do is on the GPUs and we don't need millions of CPUs beyond these GPUs, so our simulations can run in the GPU inference and training and so on. So we have some good architectures for that. I think the LM companies now have kind of the problems that we had many years ago where they need sandboxes running on CPUs like simulating computers and so on, and we're trying to not put ourselves in that situation.
turns.zh: 对。所以正如我之前提到的，我们非常幸运拥有这些算力。到今年年底，我们将成为 GCP 上最大 GPU 集群的首批客户。实际上，现在已经启动一个月了。所以我们非常幸运，我实际上对现在获得算力的初创公司感到相当难过，因为变得越来越难。但是的，所以我们有这个非常大的集群，基于 GPU，比如 Nvidia GPU，这对我们来说非常幸运，因为这意味着我们可以轻松地进行模拟、训练和推理。它们是非常通用的芯片，所以很棒。我认为特别是 Rubin 芯片，它们有一种架构，一个机架基本上可以被视为一台机器。一个机架内的节点之间有非常高的带宽，这对于强化学习非常重要，因为强化学习需要非常快的迭代周期，而 LLM 相对而言相当慢。所以这对我们来说非常幸运。我认为我们 8-10 年前在 Google 做的一些事情，当时我们基本上有丰富的 CPU，那已经不再适用了。所以我们真的需要确保我们所做的一切都在 GPU 上，我们不需要在这些 GPU 之外还需要数百万个 CPU，这样我们的模拟可以在 GPU 推理和训练等上运行。所以我们有一些好的架构。我认为 LM 公司现在有我们多年前遇到的问题，他们需要在 CPU 上运行沙箱，比如模拟计算机等，我们正试图不让自己陷入那种情况。

turns.en: All the compute, is it roughly fungible between the different things that you're doing? I imagine you're building crucibles and then you're kind of doing these big rollouts where the agents are actually learning. Is that the rough buckets of what compute is being used for?
turns.zh: 所有的算力，在你正在做的不同事情之间大致可以互换吗？我想象你在构建熔炉，然后进行这些大型部署，智能体实际上在学习。这是算力被用于的大致分类吗？

turns.en: Yeah, you could split it up into training, inference, and simulation.
turns.zh: 是的，你可以把它分为训练、推理和模拟。

turns.en: Is the same compute equally good at training, inference, and simulation?
turns.zh: 同样的算力在训练、推理和模拟上同样出色吗？

turns.en: No.
turns.zh: 不。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: So I think it's pretty clear what has happened with GPUs over the last many years or since deep learning took off is that they've been more and more tailored towards training, and maybe in the last few years also inference, but less about simulation. So but we are similarly to the LLM companies, we also want to be in the case where scaling laws matter. Like we know that roughly if you add this amount of compute and experiences, then we get a certain amount of quality out of that.
turns.zh: 所以我认为很明显，过去许多年或自深度学习兴起以来，GPU 发生的情况是它们越来越针对训练，也许在过去几年也针对推理，但较少针对模拟。但类似于 LLM 公司，我们也希望处于缩放定律重要的境地。就像我们知道大致上如果你增加这么多算力和经验，那么我们就能从中获得一定质量。

turns.en: So I guess if GPUs aren't great for scaling simulation, then what's the solution?
turns.zh: 所以我猜如果 GPU 不擅长扩展模拟，那么解决方案是什么？

turns.en: Right. So there are many different solutions here. There's model-based reinforcement learning where the model becomes much more expensive compared to the simulation. So there are many different tricks you can do. There are various approaches for replay buffers or reusing data many times. So there are ways around that. And other than that, we do spend quite some effort on just making the simulations as fast as possible and making them use the best use of the GPUs.
turns.zh: 对。所以这里有许多不同的解决方案。有基于模型的强化学习，其中模型变得比模拟昂贵得多。所以你可以做许多不同的技巧。有各种方法用于回放缓冲区或多次重用数据。所以有办法绕过这一点。除此之外，我们确实花了不少精力让模拟尽可能快，并让它们最好地利用 GPU。

turns.en: Are you seeing scaling laws yet or is it too early to say?
turns.zh: 你看到缩放定律了吗，还是说为时过早？

turns.en: So for reinforcement learning, scaling laws are slightly different, right? So scaling laws is the component of how much compute you put in, how much data you put in, and the model size. Well, reinforcement learning is a little bit different because the problem is non-stationary, so as you progress in the problem, the data changes, the data distribution changes. So they are a little bit different. It's a very interesting research direction.
turns.zh: 所以对于强化学习，缩放定律略有不同，对吧？缩放定律是投入多少算力、投入多少数据以及模型大小的组成部分。强化学习有点不同，因为问题是非平稳的，所以随着你在问题中的进展，数据会变化，数据分布会变化。所以它们有点不同。这是一个非常有趣的研究方向。

turns.en: I understand they're different, but are you seeing some sort of scaling law where more compute in gets you closer to achieving the goals, or is it hard to say right now?
turns.zh: 我理解它们不同，但你是否看到某种缩放定律，即投入更多算力能让你更接近实现目标，还是现在很难说？

turns.en: Yeah, but it's something we are actively pushing towards. And especially as we transition from a smaller cluster to the bigger cluster, we want to be ready for that.
turns.zh: 是的，但这是我们正在积极推动的事情。特别是当我们从较小的集群过渡到更大的集群时，我们希望为此做好准备。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: David, when he introduced you, he mentioned that you had done some very foundational work on compute and algorithms for reinforcement learning upon which the field really relies on today. Maybe talk about some of that work, and in particular your work around IMPALA and SEED. What are those, and how do they relate to the work that you're doing at Ineffable?
turns.zh: David，他介绍你时提到，你在强化学习的算力和算法方面做了一些非常基础性的工作，这个领域今天真的依赖这些工作。也许可以谈谈其中一些，特别是你在 IMPALA 和 SEED 上的工作。它们是什么，以及它们与你目前在 Ineffable 所做的工作有何关联？

turns.en: Right. So when I joined the deep learning team at DeepMind, most people were running single-machine CPU-based reinforcement learning. So the scale was quite small. What I did together with colleagues was to make a reinforcement learning agent that really utilized GPUs. It could scale linearly with compute. I think partially because it was very efficient, it was very good at scaling. And the third thing was it was very easy to extend and modify and do whatever you wanted with it. It contributed to it being the most popular reinforcement agent at the company, and I think at one point most RL teams used it or derivatives of it. So that was quite successful and quite a nice project to work on.
turns.zh: 对。当我加入 DeepMind 的深度学习团队时，大多数人都在运行单机 CPU 的强化学习。所以规模相当小。我和同事一起做的是，打造一个真正利用 GPU 的强化学习智能体。它可以随算力线性扩展。我认为部分原因是它非常高效，非常擅长扩展。第三点是它非常容易扩展和修改，你想怎么用就怎么用。这使它成为公司里最受欢迎的强化学习智能体，我记得有一段时间大多数强化学习团队都在用它或它的衍生版本。所以那相当成功，也是一个很不错的项目。

turns.en: Then later on, we got TPUs, right? We got racks of these TPUs, so we needed to scale beyond that. So some of my work at Google Brain after I left DeepMind to found the Google Brain Amsterdam office was to scale to racks of TPUs, and that product was called SEED RL. So it was really about utilizing the TPUs both for inference and training in the best possible way while keeping the environments as flexible as you wanted them to be. It could be anything from Go to very expensive physics simulations.
turns.zh: 后来，我们有了 TPU，对吧？我们有了成架的 TPU，所以需要扩展到更大规模。所以我在离开 DeepMind 去创立 Google Brain 阿姆斯特丹办公室后，在 Google Brain 的部分工作就是扩展到成架的 TPU，那个产品叫 SEED RL。所以它真的是关于以最佳方式利用 TPU 进行推理和训练，同时保持环境尽可能灵活。它可以是任何东西，从围棋到非常昂贵的物理模拟。

turns.en: And how's that being used at Ineffable?
turns.zh: 那在 Ineffable 是怎么用的？

turns.en: Yeah. So well we actually implemented a few of those algorithms. Also derivatives of these algorithms. So that is what we are using today. We have, depending on the environments, we use different algorithms, right? That have pros and cons between them. So yeah, so we talked about we have some very simple, fast to assemble environments and also some that are more expensive.
turns.zh: 是的。我们实际上实现了其中一些算法。还有这些算法的衍生版本。所以这就是我们今天在用的。我们根据环境不同，使用不同的算法，对吧？它们各有优缺点。所以是的，我们谈到过，我们有一些非常简单、快速组装的环境，也有一些更昂贵的。

turns.en: For those who are working on large-scale RL architectures today and haven't read those original papers, it's definitely worth a look because I think you'll discover that many of the ideas that are currently in use kind of trace back to those early work that Lassa kind of did and figured out, which was a little bit prescient, I would say. I think it's actually kind of fun to see the reinforcement learning space now versus like 10 years ago or like let's say like eight years ago maybe. The LLM community is also using reinforcement learning in particular last two years. And a lot of the things that they're using are being rediscovered approaches that we used many years ago. So that's kind of interesting to see with a lot of novelty as well on top of it, right? But yeah,
turns.zh: 对于那些今天在做大规模强化学习架构、还没读过那些原始论文的人，绝对值得一看，因为我想你会发现，当前使用的许多想法都可以追溯到 Lassa 早期所做和弄明白的工作，我会说那有点先见之明。实际上，看到现在的强化学习领域与 10 年前或比如 8 年前相比，我觉得挺有趣的。LLM 社区也在使用强化学习，尤其是过去两年。他们使用的很多东西都是我们多年前用过的、正在被重新发现的方法。所以看到这些挺有意思的，而且上面还有很多新颖之处，对吧？但是的，

turns.en: Can you talk a little bit about your team? How big is the team right now?
turns.zh: 你能稍微谈谈你的团队吗？团队现在有多大？

turns.en: We have intentionally kept the team relatively small. So we're not in a hurry to build a giant organization. I think you can do an awful lot nowadays with a small number of incredibly talented people. So we have hired 20 people in total. And yeah, the people we've hired, it's about finding some of the exceptionally talented people, but it's not just about talent for us. It's also about bringing together people who are kind, collaborative human beings. That's really important to the kind of culture we're trying to build, and people who are really well aligned with the kind of mission that we're following. And people that sort of fit the needs that we have. So we try and build the team with the right set of skills as well. So all of those four things are really important, and yeah, we kind of have very high standards and very high expectations of the people that come in. So we'll be very lucky to get some amazing, really amazing people. And so just to tie it to the compute as well, right? Like this relatively small amount of people so far means that we have a lot of compute per person, right? And like these days you can do a lot of experiments just like one person. So it's really also to keep the compute to person ratio quite high.
turns.zh: 我们有意保持团队相对较小。所以我们不急于建立一个庞大的组织。我认为如今用一小群极其有才华的人就能做非常多的事。所以我们总共雇了 20 人。是的，我们雇的人，是要找到一些特别有才华的人，但对我们来说不仅仅是才华。还要把善良、乐于合作的人聚在一起。这对我们试图建立的文化非常重要，还有那些与我们追随的使命高度一致的人。以及那些符合我们需求的人。所以我们试图用合适的技能组合来组建团队。所以这四件事都非常重要，是的，我们对进来的人有非常高的标准和非常高的期望。所以我们很幸运能得到一些很棒的、真正很棒的人。那么，也把它和算力联系起来，对吧？到目前为止相对较少的人意味着我们人均算力很高，对吧？而且如今一个人就能做很多实验。所以这也是为了保持算力与人员的比例相当高。

turns.en: So we're not like fighting for resources from day one.
turns.zh: 所以我们不是从第一天起就争抢资源。

turns.en: I think three of the co-founders worked together on AlphaStar. Many of you did work together. Are you assembling the Avengers, especially given the recent changes from DeepMind? Are you assembling the Avengers of folks that you've worked with in the past? Have you hired new people? And if so, what are the attributes that make somebody new to you likely to be a fit at Ineffable?
turns.zh: 我想有三位联合创始人一起在 AlphaStar 上工作过。你们很多人确实一起工作过。你是在组建复仇者联盟吗，尤其是考虑到 DeepMind 最近的变化？你是在组建你过去共事过的人的复仇者联盟吗？你雇了新的人吗？如果是，是什么特质让一个你不认识的人有可能适合 Ineffable？

turns.en: So it's a mixture. So, I mean, AlphaStar was an exceptional team. It was sort of intentionally assembled within DeepMind by choosing the best of the best to work on that project. So in some sense it's not a surprise that I think actually four of our co-founders come from that team. But we are not exclusively drawing from that team or indeed from DeepMind. I mean the other three founders all came from very successful startups. And we hire people who are brilliant but also kind and nice people to have around, who are going to work together well, who are aligned with the mission, and who fit the things that we need. So, but in terms of finding those people, we put a lot of effort into getting the right people. So, as uncomfortable as it is, I've had to say no to a lot of people I've worked with in the past just because our bar is so super high. You know, I've been fortunate to work with some amazing people. And so, you know, I've been choosing amongst a very exceptional crop and bringing in what I consider to be a superstar team. And so yeah, it's not easy to get into Ineffable, but the people who we have are wonderful human beings and yeah, very very proud of the people we brought in.
turns.zh: 所以是混合的。我的意思是，AlphaStar 是一支非凡的团队。它是在 DeepMind 内部有意组建的，挑选最优秀的人来做那个项目。所以从某种意义上说，我认为实际上我们有四位联合创始人来自那个团队，这并不奇怪。但我们并不只从那个团队或 DeepMind 招人。我的意思是，另外三位创始人都来自非常成功的初创公司。我们雇的人很聪明，但也善良、好相处，能很好地合作，与使命一致，并且符合我们需要的东西。所以，但在找到这些人方面，我们付出了很多努力来找到合适的人。所以，尽管不舒服，但我不得不拒绝很多过去共事过的人，因为我们的标准太高了。你知道，我有幸与一些了不起的人共事。所以，你知道，我一直在非常杰出的一批人中挑选，带进来我认为是超级明星的团队。所以是的，进入 Ineffable 不容易，但我们有的人都是很棒的人，是的，非常非常为我们带来的人感到骄傲。

turns.en: I can see why people are drawn to working at Ineffable, especially at a time when the biggest clusters, the biggest labs are locked in this prisoner's dilemma race, and there's a lot of dollars at stake, so decisions get made differently. I can imagine for a set of people that really deeply believe in the scientific mission of what you want to accomplish, this must feel like a breath of fresh air.
turns.zh: 我能理解为什么人们被吸引到 Ineffable 工作，尤其是在最大的集群、最大的实验室陷入这种囚徒困境竞赛的时候，有很多钱在赌注上，所以决策方式不同。我可以想象，对于一群真正深信你们想要完成的科学使命的人来说，这一定感觉像一股清风。

turns.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为是这样。

turns.en: And we've tried to establish a research-led culture. So it's not a company that's led by building an incremental next product, V17.1 on the thing that's come before. It's a company that's built on researchers pursuing their passion and trying to produce the breakthroughs that they believe are possible. And we center the company around that from the beginning and from the outset to create a haven for research, where we push back on product pressure because we believe that if we make these breakthroughs, it will lead to far bigger products downstream and far bigger successes than if we kind of start off from day one on, oh, here's the product we're doing from the beginning. So, yeah, so it's research-led. We're creating, I think, a really special environment and yeah, people are loving it. I'm loving it.
turns.zh: 我们试图建立一种以研究为主导的文化。所以，这不是一家由打造增量式下一个产品（比如在已有产品上推出 V17.1）所驱动的公司。这是一家建立在研究人员追求他们的热情、并试图产生他们认为可能的突破之上的公司。我们从一开始就把公司围绕这一点来构建，创造一个研究的避风港，在这里我们顶住产品压力，因为我们相信，如果我们取得这些突破，它将在下游带来比从一开始就做产品大得多的产品和成功。所以，是的，这是以研究为主导的。我认为我们正在创造一个非常特别的环境，是的，人们很喜欢它。我也很喜欢。

turns.en: Wonderful, wonderful. I'd love to close with some predictions, maybe, especially since you're such a super forecaster. What's your guess for when you'll have the first strong evidence that the approach is working and then what's your forecast for when we'll achieve the mission that you've set out to achieve this first contact with super intelligence?
turns.zh: 太棒了，太棒了。我想以一些预测来结束，也许，特别是因为你是一位超级预测者。你猜什么时候你会获得第一个强有力的证据表明这种方法有效，然后你预测我们什么时候会实现你所设定的使命——首次接触超级智能？

turns.en: Yeah, so these are fair questions. So there are going to be some reasonable bars of uncertainty on this.
turns.zh: 是的，这些都是合理的问题。所以在这方面会有一些合理的不确定性。

turns.en: Yeah, but you're being recorded, so we're going to hold you to it.
turns.zh: 是的，但你正在被录音，所以我们会让你兑现的。

turns.en: Exactly. Yeah. So I think we will see some extremely strong evidence that we're on the right track within a year and I think we will achieve something which is a true super intelligence like the according to the definition I gave earlier of something which discovers things which are far beyond what humans can achieve in across everything from science, mathematics, technology, languages etc etc. I originally thought within three to five years. My timelines have accelerated a little bit. So I'm gonna say three years because of yeah what can be done with like coding agents to accelerate things.
turns.zh: 没错。是的。所以我认为我们将在一年内看到一些极其强有力的证据表明我们走在正确的轨道上，我认为我们将实现真正的超级智能，就像我之前给出的定义那样，即发现远远超出人类在科学、数学、技术、语言等各个领域所能实现的东西。我原本认为在三到五年内。我的时间线加快了一点。所以我会说三年，因为是的，编码智能体可以加速事情。

turns.en: I think yeah I think things are going to move fast.
turns.zh: 我认为，是的，我认为事情会发展得很快。

turns.en: Buckle up. It's going to be a journey.
turns.zh: 系好安全带。这将是一段旅程。

turns.en: Wonderful. Lei David, this is a wonderful wonderful conversation. I'm so inspired by what you're building and thank you for taking the time to sit down and share with our audience what you're building today.
turns.zh: 太棒了。David，这是一次非常精彩的对话。你所构建的东西让我深受启发，感谢你抽出时间坐下来与我们的观众分享你今天正在构建的东西。

turns.en: Thank you, Sonia. Pleasure.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，Sonia。很荣幸。

tldr.en: Superintelligence will emerge from systems that learn autonomously from experience, not from human data.
tldr.zh: 超级智能将诞生于从经验中自主学习的系统，而非依赖人类数据。

tldr.en: Simulation is the safest and fastest place to build and understand superintelligence.
tldr.zh: 模拟是构建和理解超级智能最安全、最快速的场所。

tldr.en: Giving up human priors and data leads to faster and greater discovery, as AlphaZero showed.
tldr.zh: 放弃人类先验和数据能带来更快、更伟大的发现，AlphaZero 已证明。

qs.en: What is a superlearner and how to build it?
qs.zh: 什么是超级学习者，以及如何构建它？

qs.en: Why give up human data and priors?
qs.zh: 为什么要放弃人类数据和先验？

qs.en: Can superintelligence be built entirely in simulation?
qs.zh: 超级智能能否完全在模拟中构建？
